title: pager-notes-ashley-2026-03-14
content:
Quick context (for my future self):
- Night shift oncall handoff at 18:30 local. Took pager at 19:00. Quiet until the spike.
- Incident: increased 5xx ratio for hosted API (text.generate) starting ~20:12, peaked 20:18. Alerts: API-5xx-rate (threshold 0.5%) triggered.

Timeline / raw notes:
- 20:12: Pager fired: API-5xx-rate (0.8% over 5m). Slack ping to #sre-pager-ops.
- 20:13: Quick check: grafana panel shows elevated 5xx concentrated on region-us-west2, route /v1/text.generate, model=redwood-open/ggml-13b. Error classes: 503 (overloaded) and 504 (gateway timeout).
- 20:15: Ran basic health check curl against one of the pool endpoints: 503 returned with body: "backend busy".
- 20:16: Looked at infra autoscaler logs (kubectl -n inference get hpa): no recent scale up events; autoscaler CPU metric at ~70%.
- 20:17: Checked serving-runtime logs (kubectl logs inference-pool-12 -n inference | tail -n 200): saw repeated OOM warnings around KV cache allocations at ~20:10 and immediate restarts.
- 20:18: Notified infra oncall (Priya) for possible capacity/OOM. Spun up a couple of spare nodes as an emergency measure: infra autoscaling override to add 2 worker GPUs (manual emergency).
- 20:22: New nodes join, pods scheduled; however some pods crash loop with same OOM. Suspected model variant or quantization mismatch introduced in last rollout.
- 20:25: Rolling back latest deployment tag for model-serving-resources (image: model-runtime:2026-03-14-canary -> previous: model-runtime:2026-03-12) via k8s rollout undo.
- 20:30: Gradual reduction in 5xx; by 20:36 rates back to baseline.
- 20:40: Confirmed customer-facing metrics normalized; closed immediate paging.

Immediate remediation actions taken:
- Manual emergency scale: +2 GPU workers in us-west2 (temp override).
- Rollback model-runtime canary to previous stable.
- Restarted failing pods to clear KV cache fragmentation (kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-pool-us-west2).

Commands I ran (for traceability):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=model-pool-us-west2
- kubectl logs -n inference model-pool-us-west2-12 -c runtime --since=1h | grep -i oom
- kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-runtime --to-revision=3 -n inference
- infra autoscaler: POST /admin/override?add=2&region=us-west2 (internal infra API)

Observations / hypotheses:
- OOMs were triggered by an unexpected increase in KV cache allocations. Two possibilities: a) canary runtime introduced different default KV cache size or b) workload pattern (longer context windows) suddenly increased memory use.
- Autoscaler did not scale up automatically quickly enough because HPA uses CPU as proxy; memory pressure from the runtime (native GPU allocations) doesn't surface to the HPA metric.
- Some model-runtime builds include heuristic changes to prefetch/cache behavior; the canary likely changed that.

Follow-ups (post-incident TODOs) - prioritize in next 48h:
- [P0] Add a memory/GPU-alloc metric to autoscaler decision pipeline (ticket SRE-487) so we can scale on memory pressure, not just CPU. Owner: Priya. ETA: EOW.
- [P0] Add a smoke test to canary rollout that exercises KV cache allocation patterns with synthetic long-context requests (simulate 8k tokens). Owner: me (Ashley) + Applied ML. Ticket: SRE-490.
- [P1] Audit model-runtime:2026-03-14-canary changes for default cache sizes / prefetch flags. Owner: Dev Eng (serving-runtime). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/522.
- [P1] Create an automated rollback policy that detects sustained 5xx increase within 5 minutes of a canary and automatically pauses rollout. Cross-team PR. Owner: Product infra.
- [P2] Add runbook section for "KV cache OOM pattern" under confluence: /display/SRE/pgw-rate-limit-runbook. I started a stub. Owner: me.
- [P2] Update alert to include regional breakdown (so we don't chase global symptoms). Owner: Observability team.

Notes for postmortem (if we need one):
- Short summary: Canary change to model-runtime triggered increased KV cache allocations, leading to OOMs and 5xx spikes in us-west2. Manual rollback and emergency scale mitigated.
- Root cause candidates: canary runtime behavioral change + autoscaler metric mismatch.
- Impact: ~24 minutes elevated error rate; some API requests retried by clients. No data leakage. Document affected customers? Check support queue.

Things I want to capture in the post incident writeup:
- Exact timeline with timestamps (I have raw Cloud logs link).
- Pod logs snippet showing OOM messages (attach in postmortem).
- Canary build diff (notes on flags/config).
- Why autoscaler didn't catch memory pressure (HPA metric limits).
- Proposed mitigations (see Follow-ups above).

Random running TODOs (personal):
- Add a small bash script to fetch last 1h of serving runtime logs for given pod name (save as ~/bin/get-runtime-logs).
- Clean up my local kubeconfig entries for old clusters (I keep hitting wrong contexts).
- Add a quick command alias for infra override calls (so I can add capacity faster).

Questions / unresolved:
- Did the canary flip a config flag for "kv_cache_prefetch=on"? Need someone from serving-runtime to confirm exact diff.
- Are there customers who saw high error rates and escalated? Check intercom/support tags SRE.
- Is there a way to detect KV cache fragmentation proactively? (Maybe we capture a histogram of allocation sizes on startup).

Slack/people notes:
- Messaged Priya and Jordan in #sre-pager-ops during incident. Priya handled infra join and scale, Jordan helped with k8s rollbacks.
- Follow up meeting scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PT to align on autoscaler changes (invite sent to infra-owner, obs-owner, serving-runtime lead).

Housekeeping (small wins):
- Incident quieted within ~20 minutes of rollback. Rollback was straightforward (k8s revision present).
- No customer data or secrets exposed; no compliance impact.

If I forget later, short reminder: prioritize adding GPU/memory signal into the autoscaler before the next canary wave.

Scratch ideation for a long-term fix (brainstorm):
- Short-term: autoscaler override + rollback policy + canary smoke test.
- Medium-term: dedicated memory-aware HPA replacement that reads cAdvisor or nvidia-smi metrics via sidecar and autoscaler controller.
- Long-term: runtime quotas per-pod with admission controller prevents single pod from allocating more than X% of GPU memory; combined with eviction strategy that favors lower-priority requests.

End of notes.

-- Ashley

(Keeping this in users so it's my personal handoff scratchpad; will formalize into shared postmortem if Leadership asks.)
